request: Tests in internal/conversation, internal/mission and internal/review fail when crew run just test: they read WS_CREW and WS_MISSION from the environment ws gives crew, so log entries are attributed to the crew (c1|t1 … where the test wants |t1 …). title: Parse stored doc refs with folders
request: ref.Parse misreads a document's stored ref when its path has a folder: records:adr/0001.md parses as repo records:adr, path 0001.md (it splits at the first slash before looking for the colon), so its Name() stays records:adr/0001.md instead of records/adr/0001.md. Callers that key the graph by it (internal/conversation/graph.go docKeys, internal/mission/records.go refKey, internal/ops/graph.go) then key a thread on a document in a folder differently from the same file named elsewhere. Only demo:README.md (no folder) is covered by internal/ref's cases. Found while adding heading anchors to ws: addresses in document-reader-contents-getting-around.

title: Hold nudges while crew wait on background work
request: Build the fix for the orchestrator nudging crew that wait on background work, as workspace-records:docs/orchestrator-nudges-crew-waiting-on-background-work.md recommends (decisions d1-d3 in debug-orchestrator-nudges-while-agent): each harness adapter reports the work its agent left running and whether the harness will wake the agent; OrchestratorTakes declines a quiet turn while there is such work, and ws holds the nudge until work nothing wakes the agent for has ended, with a backstop for work that never ends. Also keep a done that is reported while background work runs, so the task notification's prompt hook doesn't clear it.

title: Say what Z means where people read it
request: Say what Z means where people read it. Design 22's Z (what has to be true for the brief's purpose to be met: the plan's ## Z, or without a plan the brief's ## Acceptance) shows bare in the web UI: the End dialog's legend is just 'Z', its intro says 'each part of Z', the endings read 'At Z, its code merged or landed', the plan card says 'ws reads it strictly: Z, …', and refusals say 'Z isn't checked right' and 'part 1 of Z'. Ending a mission, I had to ask what Z is. Use a label that explains itself where people read it ('Done when', or 'Acceptance', what it's made from without a plan), and keep Z as the name in code, the design and the plan's syntax unless the brief decides otherwise. In the same message: the End dialog's refusal shows the CLI's --met syntax with a made-up repo ('1: go test passes in api/x', internal/mission/ending.go) and runs its list together in one paragraph; in the web UI it should point at the empty How boxes. Where: web/src/mission/Ending.tsx, the plan card in web/src/mission/Mission.tsx, internal/mission/ending.go, ws mission conclude's help in internal/cli/mission_signals.go, and wherever the CLI prints Z.

Clear WS_CREW/WS_MISSION in those tests (t.Setenv), or for the package.

title: Tests in internal/ops sign their commits through the user's global git config (1…

title: ws upgrade (and a new just build) leaves the running daemon on the old binary: n…
request: ws upgrade (and a new just build) leaves the running daemon on the old binary: now that the daemon has no idle timeout (daemon-idle-timeout-of-3-hours), it no longer idles out and restarts from the new ws, so a daemon of the same protocol keeps the old code until ws daemon stop. ws upgrade could stop or restart it (or say to), or a command could notice a daemon older than itself.
